ig_caption:
The Eiffel Tower took 2 years, 18,038 iron parts and 2.5 million rivets. Here's how it was built, in 60 seconds. ⏱️

Caissons sunk beside the Seine. Cranes that crawled up the legs. Hydraulic jacks nudging 4 legs into perfect alignment.

And the twist: it was supposed to be torn down after 20 years. Radio saved it. 📡

Which wonder should we build next? 👇

yt_title: How the Eiffel Tower Was Built: 2 Years in 60 Seconds #shorts
yt_description:
18,038 iron parts. 2.5 million rivets. About 300 workers on site. Compressed-air caissons beside the Seine, creeper cranes climbing the legs, and hydraulic jacks to line the legs up at the first level.

It was only meant to stand for 20 years. It was kept because it was so useful for radio.

The Eiffel Tower (1887–1889), built in 60 seconds. Which wonder should we build next?

Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiffel_Tower · https://www.toureiffel.paris/en/the-monument/key-figures
Figures are historical estimates. Animation is a stylised reconstruction.
